newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF denies asking firms to buy shares.
newsitem.headline: AGF denies asking firms to buy shares.

text.p: French insurer AGF denied on Friday a magazine article claiming it had asked bank Societe Generale and holding company Paribas to buy up its shares to thwart any takeover bid.
"We deny ever asking Societe Generale or Paribas to pick up every share in sight," a spokesman for the group said.

The weekly magazine Nouvel Economiste said Societe Generale and Paribas, already shareholders in AGF, had been buying up AGF shares at the insurer's request over the past few weeks to protect it from predators.
AGF's share price had been rising amid speculation that it could be the target of a bid, notably by Allianz AG of Germany.

But the shares closed down 3.03 percent at 208.0 francs on Friday as market talk faded that AGF could expect a bid and instead focused on chances it might make an acquisition instead, possibly of troubled rival GAN.
Societe Generale raised its stake in AGF to six percent from five percent recently but that was its own decision, the AGF spokesman said. Paribas' stake has remained stable at 2.7 percent.

AGF chairman Antoine Jeancourt-Galignani said on Thursday when announcing the group's 1996 results that other major shareholders, Groupe Suisse and state-owned nuclear materials group Cogema, had increased their holdings in the insurer too.

Groupe Suisse had raised its stake to six percent from 3.7 percent and Cogema had upped its holding to five percent from four percent. AMB holds five percent while three to four percent of AGF's capital are held by funds managed by the insurer.

Jeancourt-Galignani said the concentration of more than a quarter of AGF's capital in "a small number of hands" could help protect it against a hostile bid which he warned would be costly in light of the recent strong rise in the company's shares.
He stated the group's desire to remain independent, saying with profits up 43 percent to 1.54 billion francs, AGF had "more reason than ever to be the second-largest player in France".

AGF has consistently argued that any attempt by Allianz to take it over could encounter considerable competition difficulties and Allianz, which wants to boost its presence in France, said earlier this week it was looking at GAN.
The AGF spokesman also denied the magazine's report that AGF was in talks with the American International Group (AIG) or Internationale Nederlanded Groep IV (ING) with the aim of seeking an alliance.
"We deny vehemently holding any talks with AIG or ING," he said.
